title: Gas laws
examples: What happens to the volume of a gas if I increase the temperature?
How does changing the pressure affect the volume of a gas?
Do I need to use Celsius or Kelvin when doing gas law calculations?

explain.say: Today we explore how gas properties relate to each other. We will look at three main gas laws. First we will look at Boyle's law.

Boyle's law states that pressure and volume are inversely proportional. This means if you increase the pressure you must decrease the volume. For example, a balloon squeezed harder takes up less space.

Next we learn about Charles's law. This law connects volume and temperature when pressure is kept constant. If you heat a gas the volume will increase. For example, a hot air balloon expands in the heat.
The combined gas law brings these together. It relates pressure, volume, and temperature simultaneously. For example, if you change all three you must use the combined gas law formula.
A crucial point is always using the absolute temperature scale. You must convert all temperatures to Kelvin before calculating. Remember that zero Kelvin is absolute zero temperature.
In real life, these laws help engineers design scuba tanks. They must know how pressure changes affect the gas volume underwater. This keeps the diver safe and functional.

faq.q: Do I have to use Kelvin for everything in gas law problems?
faq.a: Yes, for gas laws, you must always use the Kelvin temperature scale. You can convert from Celsius by adding 273.15 to the Celsius reading.
asks: What temperature scale should I use?
How do I change Celsius to Kelvin?

faq.q: If I only change the temperature, how does that affect the volume?
faq.a: If you only change the temperature while keeping pressure constant, the volume changes proportionally. This is described by Charles's law.
asks: What is the relationship between V and T?
How does heating a gas affect its space?

faq.q: What does 'inversely proportional' mean for Boyle's law?
faq.a: It means that as one value increases, the other value decreases by a corresponding amount. For Boyle's law, if pressure goes up, volume must go down.
asks: If P goes up, what happens to V?
How are P and V related?

faq.q: Does the combined gas law always work?
faq.a: The combined gas law applies to a fixed amount of gas undergoing changes in P, V, and T. It is a very useful general formula.

faq.q: What is the difference between the gas laws and ideal gas behavior?
faq.a: The gas laws describe ideal gas behavior, which is a simplified model. Real gases behave slightly differently due to molecular interactions.
asks: Are real gases the same as ideal gases?
What is the limitation of the gas laws?

facts: Boyle's law relates pressure and volume at constant temperature.
Charles's law relates volume and temperature at constant pressure.
The absolute temperature scale uses Kelvin, where zero is absolute zero.
The combined gas law combines these relationships for P, V, and T.

quiz.say: A gas occupies a volume of ten liters at one atmosphere of pressure. If the temperature is kept constant, and the pressure is doubled, what will the new volume be?
quiz.show: Original: 10 L, 1 atm. New P: 2 atm. New V: ?
quiz.why: Boyle's law shows inverse proportionality; doubling the pressure halves the volume.

wrong.1: This incorrectly assumes that pressure and volume are directly proportional.
wrong.2: This suggests that changing the pressure has no effect on the volume.
wrong.3: This uses a mathematical relationship that is not described by the gas laws.

quiz.say: If a gas sample has a volume of twenty cubic meters at 300 Kelvin and one atmosphere of pressure. If the pressure is kept constant, and the temperature increases to 600 Kelvin, what is the new volume?
quiz.why: Charles's law shows direct proportionality; doubling the temperature doubles the volume.

wrong.0: This incorrectly assumes that temperature has no effect on the volume.
wrong.1: This incorrectly uses the ratio of pressures instead of temperatures.
wrong.2: This incorrectly squares the temperature change factor.

quiz.say: A gas is kept at 2 atmospheres of pressure and 10 liters volume. If the temperature is increased from 300 Kelvin to 600 Kelvin, what is the new volume?
quiz.why: Using the combined gas law, the volume increases by a factor of two due to the temperature doubling.

wrong.0: This incorrectly multiplies the volume change from temperature and pressure.
wrong.1: This incorrectly assumes that the temperature change cancels out the pressure change.
wrong.3: This only considers the pressure change and ignores the temperature change.
